daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Partai Ummat signaled its willingness to cooperate with the Democratic Party on electoral reform, attending the party's 25th anniversary celebration to discuss the electoral law bill. The gesture reflects growing inter-party dialogue on legislative priorities as coalition dynamics evolve. Meanwhile, Democratic Party leader AHY's anniversary address was noted for demonstrating "the art of disagreement" in political discourse.

  • Former Minister of Religious Affairs Yaqut Cholil came under scrutiny at trial as a Kemenag employee testified that the 50:50 division of additional hajj quotas was Yaqut's policy decision.
  • In a corruption trial, former Minister Dito Ariotedjo acknowledged President Jokowi's role behind the additional hajj quota allocation, while the defense team requested Jokowi be summoned as a witness.
  • The Constitutional Court heard the DPR argue that detention requirements in the new Criminal Procedure Code are more humane and uphold human rights.
  • A regional official in West Sumatra admitted in court that she ordered the dismissal of a street sweeper who supported her opponent during a regional election.
  • The West Java regional secretary confirmed that the sexual harassment case involving the Sumedang deputy regent will proceed through legal channels.
  • The KPK searched a luxury house belonging to a police member in connection with the Bekasi regent bribery case, while separately the agency questioned an immigration official in a visa extortion case.
  • Kompas examined the constitutional hurdles in disqualifying a sitting vice president from office.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia called for a ceasefire and diplomatic resolution as the Yemen crisis escalated, with the Foreign Ministry urging dialogue and peaceful diplomacy amid reports that Houthi forces had captured the strategic port city of Mokha. The escalation in Yemen prompted Indonesia to reiterate its longstanding position advocating peaceful conflict resolution in Middle Eastern disputes.

  • Indonesia advocated for stronger international support for small-scale fishers during interventions at the UN Food and Agriculture Organization.
  • Japan deployed three Chinook helicopters to assist Indonesia's wildfire response, with BNPB confirming the aircraft will support firefighting operations for 21 days, with test flights already completed.
  • Indonesia sought to strengthen strategic port connectivity corridors during the Indonesia-Malaysia-Thailand Growth Triangle forum.
  • Kadin Indonesia pursued deeper economic ties with Sweden through EU trade agreements and OECD engagement.
  • On the 81st anniversary of the Indonesian Navy, analysts warned that defence procurement cannot rely solely on ship additions, while a separate piece examined maritime defence challenges across Indonesia's vast archipelagic waters.

Other

The Badan Gizi Nasional is evaluating 172 school meal providers in Pati regency after hundreds of children suffered food poisoning from the national school meal program, prompting debate over whether negligent providers should face criminal charges for repeated incidents. BGN has already removed 1,653 schools from the program, mostly private international institutions, while families in Karo filed legal complaints against BGN and providers.

  • The Prosecutor's Office is investigating alleged corruption in the school meal program, having examined six witnesses including state enterprise directors from 2017, and one official testified that only Lodewyk Pusung objected to the Rp 6 million daily budget.
  • Vice President Gibran conducted late-night inspections of peatland wildfires in Kubu Raya and ordered medical care for smoke-affected orangutans, while the BNPB head reported to President Prabowo that wildfires were deliberately set, citing farmers paid Rp 500,000 to burn land.
  • Gibran also met families of firefighters who died battling the blazes, while authorities extinguished 421 hectares of fires across six provinces and deployed a medical taskforce for 113,000 acute respiratory infection cases.
  • Search and rescue teams recovered an unmarked life jacket and a navigation buoy while searching for five journalists and crew missing in the Sunda Strait, with local fishermen joining the search.
  • Indonesia's mining revenue increased substantially as commodity prices rose, and the government announced that village cooperative managers' salaries will be paid from the state budget for two years.
  • The Indonesian Ulema Council pardoned a cleric accused of blasphemy but requested legal proceedings continue, and a deputy communications minister stated Indonesia has the foundation to develop advanced AI.
